name: Constraint-First Q with Orthogonal Kinetic Khronon
claimed_mechanism: The MOND force law is enforced by the constraint C_M = D_i[mu(y)D^i q] - rho = 0, which is lapse-weighted to maintain the constraint algebra and avoid the lapse-weighting kill. The preferred-frame sector is a degenerate khronon N with a screened coupling to the acceleration, ensuring PPN parameters scale as e^-y. Crucially, the kinetic normalization of the propagating tensor modes is controlled by an independent, unscreened R3 + K_ij term, separating the screened PPN response from the kinetic normalization to avoid P7 strong coupling.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the constraint fixes q to generate the MOND-enhanced Newtonian potential. The screened khronon coupling gives alpha_1, alpha_2 ~ e^-y, which is exponentially suppressed in the Solar System. The tensor modes have a healthy, unscreened kinetic term, ensuring c_T = 1 and no strong coupling in the MOND-off limit. Lensing is generated by the constraint-induced potential and the preferred-frame carrier, matching the dynamics.
inequivalence_argument: This candidate is inequivalent to DC-001 because it includes a screened preferred-frame coupling (N with a_mu) and a khronon field, satisfying the lensing escape requirement. It is inequivalent to DC-010 (finite-alpha_inf khronometric) because the kinetic normalization is independent of the screened coupling, avoiding the P7 strong-coupling wall. It is inequivalent to the khronometric survivor because it uses a constraint-first MOND realization (q) rather than an auxiliary-Legendre chi, and the degenerate khronon is coupled only to acceleration, not to the full spatial metric, altering the DOF structure and constraint algebra.
